<h>Lectio 1</h>
De Epístola prima beáti Ioánnis Apóstoli
<r>1 Ioannes 4:10-14</r>
<n>10</n> In hoc est cáritas: non quasi nos dilexérimus Deum, sed quóniam ipse prior diléxit nos, et misit Fílium suum propitiatiónem pro peccátis nostris.
<n>11</n> Caríssimi, si sic Deus diléxit nos: et nos debémus altérutrum dilígere.
<n>12</n> Deum nemo vidit umquam. Si diligámus ínvicem, Deus in nobis manet, et cáritas eius in nobis perfécta est.
<n>13</n> In hoc cognóscimus quóniam in eo manémus, et ipse in nobis: quóniam de Spíritu suo dedit nobis.
<n>14</n> Et nos vídimus, et testificámur quóniam Pater misit Fílium suum Salvatórem mundi.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Si oblítus fúero tui, allelúia, obliviscátur mei déxtera mea:
* Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Super flúmina Babylónis illic sédimus et flévimus, dum recordarémur tui, Sion.
<r>℟.</r> Adhǽreat lingua mea fáucibus meis, si non memínero tui, allelúia, allelúia.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the first letter of St. John the Apostle
<r>1 John 4:10-14</r>
<n>10</n> In this is charity: not as though we had loved God, but because he hath first loved us, and sent his Son to be a propitiation for our sins.
<n>11</n> My dearest, if God hath so loved us; we also ought to love one another.
<n>12</n> No man hath seen God at any time. If we love one another, God abideth in us, and his charity is perfected in us.
<n>13</n> In this we know that we abide in him, and he in us: because he hath given us of his spirit.
<n>14</n> And we have seen, and do testify, that the Father hath sent his Son to be the Saviour of the world.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> If I forget thee, Alleluia, let my right hand forget me.
* If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> By the rivers of Babylon there we sat down and wept, when we remembered thee, O Zion.
<r>℟.</r> If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, alleluia, alleluia.

b.a41f8f8366:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uarto Nonas Maii Luna vicésima octáva. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ Litaníæ minóres ad sanctum Ioánnem in Lateráno.
<h>A</h>pud Ostia Tiberína sanctæ Mónicæ, beáti Augustíni matris, cuius ille præcláram vitam, in libro nono Confessiónum, testátam relíquit.
<h>I</h>n metállo Phennénsi Palæstínæ natális beáti Silváni, Gazæ Epíscopi, qui, in Diocletiáni Imperatóris persecutióne, Galérii Maximiáni Cǽsaris mandáto, cum plúrimis suis Cléricis, martýrio coronátus est.
<h>H</h>ierosólymis sancti Cyríaci Epíscopi, qui, cum loca sancta visitáret, ibídem, sub Iuliáno Apóstata, cæsus est.
<h>C</h>ameríni sancti Porphýrii, Presbýteri et Mártyris, qui, sub Décio Imperatóre et Antíocho Prǽside, cum plúrimos (in quibus fuit Venántius) ad Christi fidem convertísset, cápite amputátus est.
<h>I</h>n metállo Phennénsi Palæstínæ sanctórum trigínta novem Mártyrum, qui, ad metálla damnáti, demum, post adustiónem candéntis ferri et ália torménta, simul cápite cæsi sunt.
<h>L</h>auréaci, in Nórico Ripénsi, sancti Floriáni Mártyris, qui, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, Aquilíni Prǽsidis iussu, in flumen Anísum, ligáto ad collum saxo, præcipitátus est.
<h>C</h>olóniæ Agrippínæ sancti Paulíni Mártyris.
<h>T</h>arsi, in Cilícia, sanctæ Pelágiæ, Vírginis et Mártyris, quæ, sub Diocletiáno Imperatóre, in bovem ǽneum candéntem inclúsa, martýrium complévit.
<h>N</h>icomedíæ natális sanctæ Antóniæ Mártyris, quæ, nímium torta et váriis afflícta cruciátibus, áltero bráchio tribus suspénsa diébus, et in cárcere biénnio deténta, ad últimum a Priscilliáno Prǽside, in confessióne Dómini, flammis exústa est.
<h>M</h>edioláni sancti Venerii Epíscopi, cuius virtútes sanctus Ioánnes Chrysóstomus, in epístola ad eum scripta, testátas relíquit.
<h>I</h>n território Petragoricénsi sancti Sacerdótis, Epíscopi Lemovicénsis.

<h>A</h>ntisiodóri sancti Curcódomi Diáconi.

b.06c76ec3a9:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>ay 4th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, the Lesser Litanies in the church of St. John Lateran.
<h>A</h>t Ostia, that is the mouth of the Tiber, [in the year 387,] the holy Monica, the mother of blessed Augustine, as to whose illustrious life he hath left unto us his witness in the ninth book of his Confessions.
<h>A</h>t the mines of Phaeno, in Palestine, the blessed Silvanus, Bishop of Gaza, who was crowned with martyrdom, [in the year 311,] along with many of his clergy, by order of the Caesar Gallerius Maximian, in the persecution under Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Jerusalem, Cyriacus, the holy Bishop [of Ancona,] who was on pilgrimage to the holy places when he was slain, under the Emperor Julian the Apostate.
<h>I</h>n Umbria, the holy martyr Porphyry, [under the Emperor Decius.]
<h>A</h>t the mines of Phaeno, in Palestine, thirty-nine holy martyrs, who had been condemned to the mines, and, after they had been scorched with red-hot iron and had endured other torments, were beheaded at the same time.
<h>A</h>t Lorck, in Austria, the holy martyr Florian. A stone was tied to his neck and he was cast into the river Enns by order of the President Aquilinus, under the Emperor Diocletian.
<h>A</h>t Cologne, the holy martyr Paulinus.
<h>A</h>t Tarsus, the holy Virgin Pelagia, who was shut up inside a bull of heated bronze, under Diocletian, and so finished her testimony.
<h>A</h>t Nicomedia, the holy martyr Antonia. She was put grievously to the torture, and afflicted with diverse sufferings. After she had been kept in prison for two years, and when she had been hung up by one arm for three days, at last the President
<h>P</h>riscilian caused her to be burnt for confessing the Lord.
<h>A</h>t Milan, [in the year 408,] the holy Venerius, Bishop of that place, as to whose excellency holy John Chrysostom hath left unto us his witness in the epistle which he wrote unto him.
<h>I</h>n the district of Perigueax, [in the year 720,] the holy Sacerdos, Bishop of Limoges.
<h>A</h>t Hildesheim, in Saxony, the holy Confessor Gothard, [Bishop of that see,] and who was numbered among the Saints by Pope Innocent II.
<h>A</h>t Auxerre, the holy deacon Curcodomus [in the third century.]
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

b.e4c16b3f67:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, a quo bona cuncta procédunt, largíre supplícibus tuis: ut cogitémus, te inspiránte, quæ recta sunt; et, te gubernánte, éadem faciámus.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.72f3d4696b:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, from Whom all good things do come, grant to us thy humble servants that by thy holy inspiration we may think those things that be good, and by thy merciful guiding may perform the same.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Commemoration of Sts. Alexander and Companions, Martyrs</r>
<r>Ant.</r> Daughters of Jerusalem, come and see the crowned martyrs, the Lord crowned them in his solemnity and delight, alleluia, alleluia.

<r>℣.</r> Precious in the sight of the Lord, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> Is the death of his saints, alleluia.

<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>G</c>rant, we beseech thee, O Almighty God, that we who do keep the birthday of thy holy servants Alexander, Eventius, Theodulus, and Juvenal, may by their prayers be delivered from all evils that presently hang over us.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
